key_insight: NeuROK learns a generative 4D neural kinematic representation that synthesizes realistic temporal deformations of objects directly from data, removing the need for hand-specified physical models or per-scene system identification.
problem_solved: Enables simulation-quality, temporally coherent deformations of static 3D objects under varied physical conditions without relying on predefined physics models or manual parameter estimation.
method: Train a generative neural representation over 4D (space + time) that encodes object shape and its plausible temporal deformations.
Condition generation on controllable factors (e.g., forces, material cues, initial state) to sample diverse, physically plausible motion trajectories.
Use data-driven learning to capture kinematic priors so new objects and scenarios can be synthesized without explicit analytical physics.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable way to add realistic temporal dynamics to 3D assets for simulation, animation, and embodied AI, reducing reliance on hand-crafted simulators and enabling richer 4D world models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data in → 4D neural kinematic model → conditioned sampling → animated 3D deformation sequence
Before/after sequence: side-by-side frames showing static object vs. generated temporal deformation
Latent-conditioning visualization: grid showing changes in output when varying force/material inputs
Metric/chart: qualitative realism or user study comparisons vs. physics-based baselines
paper_authors: Chen Geng, Guangzhao He, Yue Gao, Yunzhi Zhang, Shangzhe Wu
